title: The Birth of Lord Rama
story: King Dasharatha of Ayodhya longs for a son and performs a sacred yajna. A divine offering is given to his queens, and in time Rama, Bharata, Lakshmana and Shatrughna are born.

title: The Arrival of Sage Vishwamitra
story: Sage Vishwamitra arrives at King Dasharatha's court and asks that Rama accompany him to protect his sacred yajna.

title: Rama Protects the Yajna
story: Rama and Lakshmana travel with Vishwamitra and protect his sacred yajna from forces that seek to disturb it.

title: Sita's Swayamvara
story: In Mithila, King Janaka announces a great challenge for Sita's swayamvara. Princes from many kingdoms gather to attempt it.

title: Rama Breaks Shiva's Bow
story: Rama approaches the mighty bow of Shiva. With divine strength, he lifts the bow and breaks it, astonishing everyone present.

title: Rama and Sita's Wedding
story: After Rama succeeds at the swayamvara, preparations begin for the wedding of Rama and Sita, bringing joy to Mithila and Ayodhya.

title: Kaikeyi's Two Boons
story: Queen Kaikeyi remembers two promises granted by Dasharatha. She asks that Bharata become king and Rama be sent into exile for fourteen years.

title: Rama Accepts Exile
story: Rama learns that he must leave Ayodhya for fourteen years. Instead of anger, he accepts the decision to protect his father's honor.

title: Sita Chooses to Follow Rama
story: Sita refuses to remain in Ayodhya while Rama lives in the forest. She chooses to accompany her husband despite the hardships ahead.

title: Lakshmana Joins Rama
story: Lakshmana decides that he cannot let Rama and Sita face the forest alone. He leaves Ayodhya with them and begins their journey.

title: The Death of King Dasharatha
story: Upon Sumantra's return to Ayodhya with the empty chariot, King Dasharatha is consumed by overwhelming grief for his exiled son. Recalling a tragic curse from his youth involving the dutiful Shravana Kumar, the heartbroken monarch breathes his last breath. Ayodhya is plunged into deep mourning, left leaderless without its king or its beloved prince.

title: Bharata Rejects the Throne
story: Summoned back to Ayodhya from his uncle's kingdom, Prince Bharata arrives to find the city submerged in sorrow and learns of King Dasharatha's death and Rama's exile. Devastated and enraged by his mother Kaikeyi's deceitful actions, Bharata fiercely rejects the kingdom offered to him. He vows to travel into the forest to bring his beloved brother Rama back to take his rightful place on the throne.

title: Bharata's Journey to Chitrakoot
story: Determined to bring Rama back to Ayodhya, Bharata sets out into the forest accompanied by the royal mothers, ministers, and a vast procession of citizens. Along the way, he meets the forest chieftain Guha, who realizes Bharata's selfless devotion and assists the procession in crossing the holy Ganges River toward Chitrakoot.

title: Bharata Meets Rama at Chitrakoot
story: Upon reaching Chitrakoot, Bharata rushes to Rama's humble hermitage and falls weeping at his elder brother's feet. Deeply moved, Rama embraces Bharata, only to be struck with grief upon learning the tragic news of King Dasharatha's passing. Together with Lakshmana and Sita, the brothers offer sacred rites and mourn the loss of their beloved father in the forest.

title: Bharata Receives Rama's Sandals
story: Bharata earnestly begs Rama to return to Ayodhya and claim his rightful throne, but Rama steadfastly refuses to break their late father's sacred vow. Accepting Rama's resolve, Bharata requests his elder brother's wooden sandals to place upon the throne as a symbol of Rama's ultimate sovereignty. Bharata vows to live as an ascetic in Nandigram and rule Ayodhya only as a humble regent until Rama completes his fourteen-year exile.

title: The Blessing of Sage Atri and Anasuya
story: Following Bharata's departure, Rama decides to leave Chitrakoot to seek deeper solitude and protect the forest sages from disturbing forces. Journeying deeper into the wilderness, the royal trio arrives at the peaceful ashram of the venerable Sage Atri and his pious wife, Anasuya. Anasuya warmly receives Sita, imparting sacred wisdom on devotion and bestowing upon her celestial garments and ornaments that will never fade.

title: Encounter with Viradha in Dandakaranya
story: Leaving Sage Atri's peaceful hermitage, Rama, Sita, and Lakshmana venture into the dense and treacherous Dandakaranya forest. They are soon ambushed by the fearsome demon Viradha, who attempts to seize Sita and overpower the brothers. Rama and Lakshmana defeat the formidable rakshasa, liberating his soul and marking their first major triumph over evil in the wilderness.

title: Sage Sharabhanga's Ascendance and Rama's Sacred Vow
story: Following the encounter with Viradha, Rama, Sita, and Lakshmana arrive at the hermitage of Sage Sharabhanga, where they witness Lord Indra departing after visiting the holy ascetic. Having waited to behold Rama before relinquishing his earthly form, Sage Sharabhanga enters the sacred fire and ascends to heaven. Moved by the sight of sages' bones slain by rakshasas, Rama solemnly vows to protect the hermits and eliminate evil from Dandakaranya.

title: Visit to Sage Sutikshna's Hermitage
story: Continuing their journey through Dandakaranya, Rama, Lakshmana, and Sita arrive at the peaceful ashram of Sage Sutikshna. The pious sage warmly welcomes the royal trio and offers them his hospitality and spiritual blessings. During their stay, Sita gently questions the necessity of bearing arms in the forest, allowing Rama to reaffirm his sacred commitment to protect the sages.

title: Meeting Sage Agastya and Receiving Divine Weapons
story: After spending nearly ten years visiting various hermitages in Dandakaranya, Rama, Lakshmana, and Sita journey to the sacred ashram of the venerated Sage Agastya. The great sage warmly welcomes them and bestows upon Rama divine weapons, including the celestial bow of Lord Vishnu, unbreakable quivers, and a glowing sword. Sage Agastya then directs the royal trio to establish their residence at Panchavati along the banks of the Godavari River.

title: Meeting Jatayu and Establishing Panchavati
story: En route to Panchavati, Rama, Lakshmana, and Sita encounter the majestic vulture king Jatayu, a dear friend of King Dasharatha, who offers his friendship and pledges to help guard Sita in the wilderness. Upon reaching the serene banks of the Godavari River, Lakshmana lovingly builds a sturdy and comfortable leaf hut for their residence. Settling into the breathtaking surroundings of Panchavati, the royal trio begins a peaceful life in their new forest home.

title: Encounter with Surpanakha
story: While living peacefully in Panchavati, Rama, Lakshmana, and Sita are approached by the demoness Surpanakha, the sister of Ravana, who becomes captivated by Rama's beauty. After both Rama and Lakshmana reject her romantic advances, an enraged Surpanakha lunges to attack Sita. Protecting Sita, Lakshmana swiftly intervenes and disfigures the demoness by cutting off her nose and ears, setting into motion the central conflict of the epic.

title: The Destruction of Khara and Dushana
story: Humiliated and disfigured, Surpanakha flees to her brother Khara in Janasthana to demand swift vengeance. Enraged, Khara marches upon Panchavati with his general Dushana and a formidable army of fourteen thousand rakshasas. Instructing Lakshmana to guard Sita in a cave, Rama single-handedly confronts and annihilates the entire demon horde, including Khara and Dushana.

title: Surpanakha Incites Ravana
story: Following the total destruction of the demon army in Janasthana, a distraught and disfigured Surpanakha flees to Lanka to inform her brother, King Ravana, of Khara's death. Enraged by the defeat, Ravana listens intently as she vividly describes Sita's peerless beauty and urges him to abduct her as the ultimate vengeance against Rama. Overcome by lust and fury, the ten-headed demon king resolves to kidnap Sita and sets off to seek the help of the sorcerer Maricha.

title: Ravana and Maricha's Conspiracy
story: Ravana arrives at Maricha's hermitage to seek his aid in abducting Sita as revenge against Rama. Maricha urgently warns Ravana of Rama's supreme might and advises against the dangerous plan, but Ravana threatens him with immediate death if he disobeys. Choosing to die at Rama's hands rather than Ravana's, Maricha reluctantly agrees to transform into a golden deer to lure Rama away from Panchavati.

title: The Golden Deer Temptation
story: Maricha assumes the form of an extraordinarily beautiful golden deer adorned with shimmering gems and grazes near the hermitage at Panchavati. Captivated by its magnificent appearance, Sita earnestly begs Rama to capture the magical creature for her. Disregarding Lakshmana's warning that the deer is a demon in disguise, Rama pursues the elusive creature deep into the forest, leaving Lakshmana behind to guard Sita.

title: Maricha's Deceptive Cry
story: Deep in the forest, Rama shoots the golden deer with a lethal arrow, forcing Maricha to revert to his true demon form. As he dies, Maricha mimics Rama's voice and cries out loudly for help to deceive Sita and Lakshmana. Hearing the distressed call, Sita is overcome with fear and compels a reluctant Lakshmana to leave her unprotected and search for Rama.

title: The Abduction of Sita
story: Taking advantage of Sita being left alone, Ravana approaches the Panchavati hermitage disguised as a harmless wandering ascetic begging for alms. Upon revealing his true terrifying form and being met with fierce resistance, the enraged demon king forcefully seizes Sita and drags her onto his golden chariot. Ignoring her frantic cries for Rama and Lakshmana, Ravana takes to the sky, speeding south toward his kingdom of Lanka.

title: Jatayu's Valiant Sacrifice
story: Hearing Sita's distressed cries from the sky, the noble vulture king Jatayu courageously intercepts Ravana to rescue her. A fierce aerial battle ensues in which Jatayu heroically shatters Ravana's golden chariot and disarms the demon king. However, Ravana ultimately severs the ancient bird's wings with his sacred sword, leaving Jatayu mortally wounded on the earth as Ravana continues his flight toward Lanka.

title: Sita's Imprisonment in Lanka
story: Upon arriving in Lanka, Ravana attempts to entice Sita by showcasing his opulent palace and immense power, but she fiercely rejects him and reiterates her devotion to Rama. Enraged by her unyielding refusal, the demon king orders her to be imprisoned in the Ashoka Vatika garden under the strict vigil of fearsome demonesses. Isolated and heartbroken, Sita steadfastly awaits Rama's rescue while enduring the torment of her captors.

title: Rama's Anguish at the Empty Ashram
story: Returning toward Panchavati after slaying Maricha, Rama meets Lakshmana on the path and immediately fears for Sita's safety. Upon reaching their hermitage and finding it desolate and empty, Rama is overcome with profound grief and despair. Heartbroken, he frantically searches the surrounding forest, desperately asking the trees, animals, and rivers if they have seen his beloved wife.

title: Jatayu's Final Message to Rama
story: Continuing their desperate search through the forest, Rama and Lakshmana discover the noble vulture Jatayu lying mortally wounded on the ground. With his dying breath, Jatayu informs Rama that Ravana abducted Sita and fled toward the south, giving the brothers their first vital clue. Heartbroken by the king's selfless sacrifice, Rama lovingly performs Jatayu's funeral rites before continuing their quest.

title: The Encounter with Kabandha
story: As Rama and Lakshmana head further south through the dense wilderness, they are suddenly ensnared by Kabandha, a monstrous demon with a single eye in his chest and immense, reaching arms. The brothers swiftly sever the monster's arms, breaking a ancient curse and releasing a celestial Gandharva who was trapped within the demonic body. In gratitude for his liberation, the divine spirit advises Rama to seek an alliance with the exiled monkey prince Sugriva at Mount Rishyamuka to locate Sita.

title: Shabari's Devotion and Liberation
story: Following Kabandha's advice, Rama and Lakshmana arrive at the hermitage of Shabari, a devout elderly ascetic who has patiently awaited Rama for years. Overwhelmed with joy, Shabari lovingly offers them wild fruits and receives Rama's blessings before shedding her mortal form to attain liberation. Reassured by her deep faith, the brothers continue toward Lake Pampa on their journey to meet Sugriva.

title: The First Meeting with Hanuman
story: As Rama and Lakshmana approach Mount Rishyamuka, the exiled Vanara king Sugriva spots them and fears they are assassins sent by his hostile brother Vali. Sugriva dispatches his wise minister, Hanuman, disguised as a young ascetic, to ascertain the brothers' true identity and intentions. Deeply moved by Rama's eloquent speech and divine presence, Hanuman reveals his true form and vows to unite Rama with Sugriva.

title: The Sacred Alliance with Sugriva
story: Carried upon Hanuman's shoulders to the peak of Mount Rishyamuka, Rama and Lakshmana are warmly introduced to the Vanara prince Sugriva. In the presence of a sacred fire lit by Hanuman, Rama and Sugriva forge an eternal pact of friendship and mutual assistance. Rama promises to slay Sugriva's tyrannical brother Vali and restore Sugriva's kingdom, while Sugriva vows to mobilize his vast forces to locate and rescue Sita.

title: Rama Proves His Might to Sugriva
story: To reassure a hesitant Sugriva of his ability to defeat the formidable Vali, Rama is asked to demonstrate his extraordinary strength. With a single effortless kick, Rama hurls the massive skeleton of the demon Dundubhi miles away, and then shoots an arrow that pierces seven mighty Sal trees, the earth, and the underworld before returning to his quiver. Deeply awed by this display of divine power, Sugriva's doubts are entirely dispelled, and he gains absolute faith in Rama's promise.

title: The First Battle Between Vali and Sugriva
story: Bolstered by Rama's extraordinary display of strength, Sugriva travels to Kishkindha and issues a thunderous challenge to his brother Vali. As a fierce duel erupts between the two, Rama is unable to fire his lethal arrow because the nearly identical brothers are indistinguishable in combat. Severely beaten, a confused Sugriva flees back to Mount Rishyamuka, where Rama explains his hesitation and promises a distinct strategy for their next confrontation.
